help.title: What are daemon settings?
help.body:
These are the values the **daemon** runs with — backup schedule, scheduler limits, gate watch windows and so on. Changes here go to the daemon, **not to this device**, and take the same road as the `aeon settings` command.

### Where a value comes from
Every setting has up to three layers, and the first that applies wins:
1. **Environment** — a variable set where the daemon starts. It always wins, so the setting is read-only here and the panel names the variable.
2. **Saved** — a value someone saved here or with the CLI. It records who changed it and when.
3. **Default** — what the feature declares. *Reset to default* removes the saved value.

An environment variable or saved value the daemon cannot use is ignored and flagged **invalid**; the next layer stays in force.

### Sensitive settings
A setting marked **sensitive** asks you to type its name before it changes.

### New settings
When a feature declares a setting it appears here on its own — nothing in this page needs to know the key.

help.title: What are backups?
help.body:
A backup is a **copy of the daemon''s database** — the one place agents, loops, memory and configuration live. Without a recent copy, a damaged disk or a bad migration could lose all of it.

### What this page shows
- **Last backup** and its state: whether a recent copy exists and the last run succeeded.
- **Next backup**: when the schedule runs again, or that it is off.
- **Database**: its size and how many migrations have been applied.

### What you can do
- **Back up now** — make a copy immediately.
- **Open a copy** — see where it came from, **verify** it, and get the exact command to restore it. A quick verify checks the file; the **full restore drill** opens it as a live store and runs its migrations — the only check that a restore would really work.
- **Prune** — remove old copies the retention settings no longer keep. You see the daemon''s plan first and type *prune* to confirm; removed copies cannot be recovered.

### Restoring
Restoring **replaces the database** and needs the daemon stopped, so it is never a button here: open a copy and run its command in a terminal.

### The schedule
How often copies are made, how many are kept and where they go are daemon settings (`backup.*`) — open them from *Schedule settings* below the cards.

help.title: What are system records?
help.body:
The app ships some content as **records the daemon keeps in its database** — agent definitions, policy rules, blueprints and so on. They are grouped in **sets**. This page shows each set and whether the copy on this machine is current with what the app ships.

### What you can do
- **Open a set** to see its records, each with the daemon''s own state and reason.
- **Plan** a set to see exactly what applying it would change. A plan is a read — nothing is written.
- **Apply** the plan. An **inert** set applies in one click after you have seen the plan. A **guard** set (one that can grant permissions) always asks you to type its id first.
- **Restore** one record that was removed, retired or changed locally. This replaces your local version with the shipped one.

### Record states
The state is the daemon''s word: *applied* (current), *behind* (a newer one is shipped), *absent*, *removed*, *diverged* (changed locally), *retired* (no longer shipped) or *failed*. The page never works out a state itself.

### New sets
When the daemon declares a new set it appears here on its own.
